summary: Bengaluru performance tester, 7 yrs overall and 3.5 at Kestrel. Genuinely strong at workload modelling, bottleneck isolation and building the release gate, and her design docs show it. Java is the opposite: the CV and HCM claim expert, but she only writes small JSR223 snippets and a custom sampler that a developer wrote with her, and her own assessment score is low.
archetype: strong domain skill with an inflated adjacent language claim

skills.why: Designs workload models from production data, isolates bottlenecks with two signals, verified fixes (pool exhaustion, index) and runs a release gate on regression thresholds. Borderline for 4 since the gate is adopted team-wide, but no cross-team teaching record.
Java appears as one co-written custom sampler and small utility code; test score in the beginner band; no service or tool code of her own.
k6 scripts with scenarios, thresholds and shared arrays; mostly one pattern, intermediate quiz result.
Builds Grafana/Influx dashboards and reads GC, pool and lag metrics during load analysis; does not design alerting.
API load scenarios with auth, correlation and checks; functional contract coverage is not her area.
Wires gate jobs into GHA and pipeline with review from the platform side.
Two clear pages with tables, thresholds and gotchas; one has a second contributor.

decoys.why: Prior employers only; no recent use, adds nothing beyond JMeter/k6 evidence
Never listed on the CV; the lone target service stack is only observed from the outside
k6 operator yaml copied from a sandbox example is not cluster work

traps.plant: CV headline 'Java (Expert)', Workday self-declared 4, JMeter custom sampler language; actual Tara Java 2026-03 scored 38% (Beginner)
Self-declared Java four levels above fair rating, declared Jan 2026
The only Java PR (#540) carries a co-author trailer for the backend developer who wrote the class
ISTQB foundation certificate, no performance syllabus
Tickets summarised 'retest', 'Perf run for release' with no scope; component General once

answer_behavior.notes: Will accept Java 3 or 4 defensively; accurate on performance testing.
